NV-governor.statusNote: Gov. Joe Lombardo (R) seeks a second term against Attorney General Aaron Ford (D). In the June 9 primary Lombardo took 91% of the Republican vote; Ford won the Democratic race with 63% over Washoe County Commissioner Alexis Hill. State Board of Education member Danielle Ford is running with no party affiliation. One of the most competitive governor races in the country. Positions researched and sourced for Danielle Ford (no party affiliation) as of Sep 2, 2026.

NV-house-1.statusNote: General election field from Nevada's June 9, 2026 primary: Dina Titus (Democrat), Carrie Buck (Republican). Rep. Dina Titus is the incumbent. Also on the November ballot with no party affiliation: Bobby Khan and Steven St John.

candidates.name: Joe Lombardo
candidates.background: Governor since 2023 after 34 years in law enforcement, including two terms as Clark County Sheriff (2015-2023). Army and Nevada National Guard veteran with UNLV degrees in civil engineering and crisis management. Won the June 9 Republican primary with 91% against six challengers.
priorities: No new taxes and lighter regulation

cost.label: On inflation: 'I can't control that', calls fix-it promises false; points instead to cutting employer taxes and eliminating over 900 regulations (Nevada Current)

health.label: Vetoed prescription drug price caps along with paid family leave and free school meals in a record 87-veto session (Nevada Current)

housing.label: Mixed: created a $250M state attainable-housing fund projected to leverage five times that in projects, paired with expedited permitting and prevailing-wage exemptions Democrats criticized (Nevada Independent)

immigration.label: Opposes sanctuary cities; as sheriff worked with ICE to identify and deport 'violent criminals' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Pledged to 'veto any new tax increase'; touts reduced employer taxes (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Withdrew Nevada from the U.S. Climate Alliance, saying its goals 'conflict with Nevada's energy policy objectives'; ordered a 'balanced approach' pairing natural gas with renewables (Nevada Independent)

education.label: Supports expanding charter schools, 'school choice, and opportunity scholarships' plus read-by-three accountability (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Opposes defunding police; pledges to 'put bad guys away' and keep communities safe (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Mixed: self-described pro-life and endorsed by National Right to Life, but signed SB 131 shielding abortion patients and providers and says he will respect Nevada's voter-approved 24-week law (CBS News)

democracy.label: Proposed to 'eliminate ballot harvesting, end universal mail ballots, require an ID to vote' (Ballotpedia)

controversies.label: Settled a four-year Nevada Ethics Commission case over campaigning in his sheriff's uniform and badge, paying $5,000 with no willful violation found after the commission's original $20,000 fine and censure were challenged in court (Nevada Independent)

candidates.name: Aaron Ford
candidates.background: Nevada Attorney General since 2019 and the first Black official elected to statewide constitutional office in Nevada; previously state Senate Majority Leader (2017-2019). A former public school math teacher from Dallas with a J.D. and Ph.D. from Ohio State, he secured over $1 billion in opioid settlements as AG. Won the June 9 Democratic primary with 65% over Alexis Hill.
priorities: 'Affordable Nevada' agenda: housing, healthcare, and energy costs
Renter protections and cracking down on corporate landlords

cost.label: Pledges to 'crack down on price gouging and fraudulent medical billing' and predatory pharmacy benefit managers; fought NV Energy's 'unlawful mandatory demand charge' (campaign site)

health.label: Targets predatory pharmacy benefit managers and fraudulent medical billing; won more than $1.2B in opioid settlements as AG (campaign site)

housing.label: Cap security deposits at one month's rent, ban junk fees, limit Wall Street purchases of single-family homes, and revive corporate-landlord bills Lombardo vetoed, while also accelerating permitting (campaign housing plan)

immigration.label: Committed to protecting Nevada's 13,000 DACA recipients from federal overreach (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Mixed: wants K-12 funding raised to the national average yet is 'not open to adding new taxes during an affordability crisis'; his team says 'he will not raise taxes period' (Nevada Independent)

climate.label: Backs 'clean and affordable energy', rooftop solar and efficiency incentives, and making data centers 'pay their fair share' for energy and water demands (campaign site)

education.label: Former math teacher who sued the Trump administration over dismantling the Department of Education to protect $1B in annual federal school funding (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed 'tough and smart on crime': funds diversion courts and mental health programs while also 'increasing penalties for criminals who attack our law enforcement officers' (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 'Abortion is health care'; pledges to 'uphold the fullest scope of Nevada's state statute protecting access to abortion' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Sued to block the Trump election order targeting mail ballots, defending Nevada's mail voting system (Nevada Current)

controversies.label: A 2026 ethics complaint over sponsored trips valued above $35,000 and campaign use of official social media advanced past initial review; IRS liens of $185,000 for 2010-2013 taxes were cleared in 2016 (Wikipedia)
